home.h1: FSD Ethiopia: Financial Sector Deepening Ethiopia

who.title: Finance that works for every Ethiopian
who.lead: We identify barriers to Ethiopia’s financial system and help fix them through technical assistance, grants, and research.

work.title: Closing Ethiopia’s finance gaps
work.lead: Our programmes widen access to financial services, open up capital for businesses and mobilise finance for climate action.

join.title: Build the financial future with us
join.lead: We hire, procure and partner openly, and publish every opportunity with its deadline.

role.title: Fixing what holds Ethiopia’s financial markets back
role.body: Established in 2022 with funding from the UK’s Foreign, Commonwealth & Development Office and the Gates Foundation, and incubated by FSD Africa, we look for the underlying causes of financial system failures and help market actors address them. Policymakers, regulators and market actors draw on our technical assistance, grants and research so that the financial sector serves a wide cross-section of Ethiopian people and businesses.

how.title: How we work
how.intro: Four tools, each aimed at a specific constraint in the market.

ta.label: Technical assistance
ta.body: We work alongside regulators, policymakers and market actors to design and deliver reforms.

grants.label: Grants
grants.body: Targeted grants help institutions test products and models the market would not yet fund alone.

research.label: Research and data
research.body: We publish research and data on access, usage and gaps, so policy and investment rest on facts.

convening.label: Convening and advocacy
convening.promise: The right people at one table.
convening.body: Summits, dialogues and our knowledge series bring the sector together to agree what to change.

boards.title: Preparing women for Ethiopia’s boardrooms
boards.body: With IFC, we have run three rounds of corporate governance training for women professionals preparing for board seats, with environmental, social and governance principles built into the curriculum.
